home.title: Sofaly · Your TV, simple again
home.description: Sofaly is the home screen for Google TV and Android TV: everything organized in a cross (Watch, Listen, Play, Apps), large text and no ads.
home.eyebrow: Home screen for Google TV and Android TV
home.lead: Sofaly replaces your TV's home screen with a tidy cross: Watch, Listen, Play and Apps, in large text and with no ads. It also looks after the house, wakes you up and talks to your phone.
home.hero_note: No account, no ads, no tracking of what you watch.
home.cross_title: One screen, four ways to go
home.cross_lead: ◀ ▶ pick a world. ▲ ▼ go through what's inside. That's it, and anyone at home learns it in a minute.

continue: Back to where you stopped: the episode, the radio station, the podcast or the app.
watch: Your video apps, your movies from the computer or a USB drive, and a player that plays everything.
listen: Radio stations from all over the world and podcasts, with a full-screen player and a sleep timer.
play: Cloud, PC and retro games in one place, with your controller already paired.
apps: The 8 you use most up front, and all the others one click away.

mock.listen_detail: Stations from all over the world, by name or country

home.why_lead: The home screen your TV came with was made to sell. Sofaly was made for your family to use.

home.why_source: Ads on the Google TV home screen: Android Authority, April 2026.
highlights: Large text, a simple mode that says the app's name, high contrast and the screen reader. In 15 languages.
The alarm turns the TV on by itself, raises the volume slowly and opens Good morning: time, weather and agenda.
Home Assistant lights, scenes and doorbell on the TV. Goes to sleep when everyone has left.
Control it, type and send messages from any phone or computer at home, protected by a PIN.
Current weather comes from the nearest airport: measured, not guessed. A 9-day forecast with one OK.
A locked backup every night, maintenance while you sleep and a diagnosis that explains what went wrong.
home.chapters_title: Everything it does, organized like it is
home.chapters_lead: More than 80 features. Pick a world to see each one explained.
home.privacy_text: Sofaly asks for no account, shows no ads and doesn't track what you watch. Settings, photos, messages and backups stay on the TV, or in an account of yours if you connect one. The TV only talks to the services you turn on, and the privacy policy lists every one.
home.dev_title: Have an app? Put it on the home screen.
home.dev_text: Sofaly already comes with ready-made cards (moon, rates, countdown, reminder). A plugin is your own Android TV app sending one more card to the home screen: the delivery order, the bus that's coming, the notice from the building. No SDK, no fee, and the app stays yours.
home.plans_title: Start free. Grow when you want.
home.plans_text: Basic already has the full home screen, the player, Listen, Play, the alarm clock and the screensaver. Pro and Ultra add the phone, the house and the family.
faq: Does it work on my TV?
It works on Google TV and Android TV, like the Chromecast with Google TV, TVs with Google TV and Android TV boxes. The compatibility page lists the tested devices.
Do I need a computer to install it?
No. Install it from Google Play on the TV itself and follow the steps with the remote.
All of them. Sofaly only replaces the home screen: Netflix, YouTube, Prime Video and the rest open as always, and the microphone button is still the Google Assistant.
No, not even on the free plan. Sofaly doesn't sell ads and doesn't track what you watch.
Does it come with channels or movies?
No. Sofaly organizes what's already yours: your apps, your files and open radio stations and podcasts.
What if I want Google's home screen back?
Just pick Google's home screen again in the TV's settings. Nothing of yours is deleted.
home.final_text: Install it, press HOME and the whole house gets it.

features_page.title: Everything Sofaly does
features_page.description: Every Sofaly feature explained: the cross home screen, Watch, Listen, Play, the house, the weather, the family, the phone and privacy.
features_page.lead: Organized the same way as the TV screen: one world at a time. Each feature's tag says which plan it starts in.

home: A tidy screen anyone understands, arranged the way you like.
watch: Your movies, your series and a home-theater player.
listen: Radio and podcasts with the same care as video.
play: All your games in one place, ready for the controller.
apps: Your apps in an order that makes sense.
house: Alarm clock, timers, automations and the connected home.
sky: The right weather and a screensaver worth leaving on.
family: A profile for everyone, care for the kids and a warm welcome for guests.
phone: The TV talks to the devices at home.
care: Backup, maintenance and diagnosis without you remembering.
everyone: Made for people who see, hear or use the remote in different ways.
privacy: No ads, no tracking, and a PIN where it matters.

cross: Continue, Watch, Listen, Play and Apps in one row. The world you pick grows big, with what's inside right below it.
◀ ▶ switch worlds, ▲ ▼ go down the column, OK opens.
continue: One place to get back to what you were doing: the episode, the station, the podcast or the last app.
It's the first item of the cross.
topbar: Search, voice, the weather in one line and the clock, always in the same place. It folds away while you browse so the screen can breathe.
quick-panel: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, sleep timer, sound output, alarm, profiles, notifications and the shopping list, from any app.
remote: HOME always comes back to Sofaly. Holding BACK opens the quick panel, holding HOME opens the House, and holding OK on an app opens its menu.
A key tester shows every button the TV receives.
now-playing: A pill at the top with the cover and title of what's playing. OK pauses or resumes, holding OK opens the app.
Turn it on in Home screen › More options.
themes: Dark, with the art of what's in focus. Gallery, with a painting from The Met every day. Sky, with satellite and map. Or a background of your own, photo or video.
Dark, Gallery and Sky in Basic; the others in Pro.
icons: Use an icon pack from Play or change a single app's icon, one by one.
Hold OK on the app › Change icon.
card-moon: Tonight's moon and how much of it is lit, worked out on the TV itself, with no internet.
A home screen card, at the end of Watch.
card-countdown: How many days are left until the date you pick, or until the next holiday.
A home screen card, at the end of Watch.
card-reminder: A note that comes back on the weekdays you choose: recycling day, medicine, a class.
A home screen card, at the end of Watch.
card-status: The TV checks an address you give it and shows whether it's up: the home server, the shop's website.
A home screen card, at the end of Watch.
card-rates: Currencies, gold and bitcoin at today's value, from an open source.
A home screen card, at the end of Watch.
card-match: When and against whom your team plays next, on a card on the home screen.
A home screen card, at the end of Watch.
plugin-cards: Besides Sofaly's own cards, partner apps put theirs on the home screen: the delivery order, the bus, the notice from the building.
Cards show at the end of Watch.
network-library: Videos, music and photos from Plex, Jellyfin, Emby, PC or NAS folders (SMB, WebDAV, FTP, SFTP, NFS), OneDrive, Dropbox, Box, Google Drive, UPnP and USB drives.
Servers that are on and USB drives show up by themselves; the rest go in Add.
player: Dolby (AC3, E-AC3), DTS and TrueHD sound, and Blu-ray, DVD and anime subtitles, without installing Kodi or VLC.
Press ▼ during a video for audio, subtitles and subtitle size.
resume: Movies and episodes come back at the right spot. The next episode starts after 10 seconds, and after 3 in a row the TV asks if you're still watching.
skip-intro: When a series' intro is known, “Skip intro · OK” shows up. You can also mark the intro once and the TV remembers.
audio-subtitles: Original with subtitles or dubbed, chosen once and remembered per title. Subtitles from the internet when the file has none.
TV and movies › Audio and subtitles.
easy-viewing: Subtitles on a black box or in yellow, “Clearer voice” that brings out speech, and “Even volume” that tames loud movies and lifts quiet ones.
auto-subtitles: When there's no subtitle in your language, the TV translates the one there is.
Pick it in the player's subtitle menu.
movie-pages: Poster, rating, cast, trailer, age rating and the movie's collection on a beautiful page, in large text.
OK on a movie or series.
lists: What you want to watch and what you've watched, synced with your account and your other devices.
Sign in with the QR in TV and movies › Services.
search: Finds movies, series, stations and apps at once, and carries the same search to YouTube, Netflix or Prime Video.
In the top bar, or by voice.
radio: Radio from all over the world
Thousands of open radio stations, by name, country or genre, with your favorites and the last ones you played.
podcasts: Subscribe by name, listen on the TV and pick the episode up where you stopped.
podcast-search: Search the whole open podcast catalog and see what's trending in your country.
podcast-player: Big cover, chapters, speed and a sleep timer that pauses at the end of the episode.
Listen › Now playing › Open the player.
phone-sound: The movie's sound goes to your phone's headphones, in sync, to watch at night without waking anyone.
games-hub: All your games in one place
GeForce NOW, Steam Link, Moonlight, PS Remote Play, RetroArch and the TV's games leave the apps row and live in Play, grouped into Cloud, From the PC, Retro and On the TV.
Hold OK on a game to change its group.
pc-games: The TV wakes the computer over the network, waits for it to answer and opens Moonlight or Steam Link.
Save the computer once in the web panel.
network-test: Tells you whether your internet can handle cloud gaming, and warns before opening a cloud game on a weak network.
controllers: Pair a controller without hunting for menus, see the connected ones at the top and, if you like, make a connected controller open Play.
game-mode: While a game is open, the screensaver, the night filter and notices wait for the match to end.
crew: See who from your Discord server is online and in which game, and call the crew right from the TV.
Turn on the server widget and paste its number.
apps-top: Apps shows the 8 apps you open most, and “All apps” brings the rest in a grid.
apps-organize: Move, stack or hide any app. Factory apps you don't use step out of the way.
app-buttons: The remote's app buttons open any app you want. Press to open, hold 3 seconds to change it.
alarm: An alarm that turns the TV on
On time, the TV turns itself on, the volume rises slowly and there's snooze. Each alarm has a name, days, a sound and a volume, even an app or the last station.
timers: Up to 3 named timers with an on-screen notice, and a stopwatch.
“Hey Google, open Remind me in 10 minutes”.
gentle-off: The sleep timer dims the screen and lowers the volume in the last 5 minutes, so nobody wakes up at the cut.
Timer tile in the quick panel.
idle-off: After the time you pick without a key press, the TV asks in large text whether you're still watching, and then sleeps.
Screen and power › Turn off when idle.
recipes: Sleep, Soap opera and Match set up the TV in one go (sound, screen and notices). One OK applies, another undoes.
automations: At a set time, when a button is pressed or when something happens (the movie paused, everyone left, rain is coming): the TV opens an app, runs a scene or turns off.
home-assistant: Lights, plugs, fans, covers, air conditioning and scenes, right from the couch. It talks to your server on your network, with no cloud in between.
doorbell: When the doorbell rings, the camera's snapshot pops up over whatever you're watching.
presence: With a UniFi router, the TV notices that the household's phones have left and goes to sleep.
voice: “Hey Google, open Weather report” reads the forecast aloud. Movies, My home, Board, timers and turning off open the same way.
weather-now: The temperature comes from the nearest airport's report, and the day/night icon follows sunrise and sunset where the TV is.
At the top of the home screen.
weather-3: The chance of rain is the median of three weather models (ECMWF, ICON and GFS), which misses less than any one of them.
Shows up in the forecast by itself.
forecast: The next 24 hours, a rain chart, 9 days, air quality, the sun and the moon.
rain-alert: A notice over your app when rain is about to start. Time to bring the laundry in.
screensaver: Greeting, a big clock, the date, the weather and cards with notifications, the next alarm and messages. In the Gallery theme, the painting of the day drifts slowly so nothing burns in.
photos: Send photos from your phone or pick a network folder. They stay in a folder only the TV can see.
A QR opens the panel on the right page.
good-morning: When you stop the alarm: greeting, time, forecast and today's agenda, and the TV can read it aloud.
calendar: Today's events and birthdays on the TV, from one account or all of them together.
OK on the date at the top.
night-filter: At night the screen gets warmer and softer on the eyes.
recap: On Sunday night, a card with screen time per app, internet used and network drops.
profiles: Each Google account on the TV has its own favorites, things to continue and app order.
kid-profile: Mark a profile as a kid's: kids mode and bedtime turn on by themselves, and leaving asks for the parents' PIN.
bedtime: During the hours you choose, only allowed apps open and the volume has a ceiling.
screen-time: A daily TV limit for whoever you choose.
guest: Hides your profile, your calendar and the apps you choose while you have visitors.
Guest tile in the quick panel.
guest-wifi: Type the password once; guests scan a QR on the TV and they're in.
family-board: Shopping list, pinned notes and today's birthdays, in the quick panel and on the screensaver.
Edit from your phone; OK ticks an item off.
family-link: Family who live far away send messages and photos to the TV at home, from anywhere.
video-message: A short video from the family shows up on the TV with the sender's name.
From the panel on the phone.
web-panel: Panel on your phone and computer
Remote control, typing with accents, a live view of the TV screen, screensaver photos, the board and backups, from the browser of any device at home.
Remote access › Sign in from the phone (QR).
ask-tv: Type or say “open YouTube”, “remind me in 7 minutes”, “turn off in 30 minutes” and the TV does it.
In the panel on the phone.
share: Installed as an app, the panel shows up in Share: a YouTube video opens on the TV, a link opens on the TV and a text becomes a message.
network-drive: The TV as a network drive
Copy files to the TV by dragging them: on Windows it shows up in This PC like a phone; on Mac, Linux and phones, over secure WebDAV.
Remote access › Show as a network drive.
windows: The TV shows up in Explorer's Network with a shortcut that opens the panel, even if its IP changes.
On whenever the panel is on.
continue-tv: Stopped in the living room? Send it to the bedroom: the other TV shows “Continue where you stopped?” and opens at the same spot.
Player menu › Send to another TV.
together: Two homes watch the same thing at the same time: pause here, it pauses there, with reactions in the corner.
homes: Look after the TV at your place and at your parents' from the same phone.
backup: While the TV is idle, a full backup locked with your password. The last 7 are kept, and every night the TV checks it would restore.
cloud-backup: Copies also go to your Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, Box, NAS or USB drive. Locked: not even the cloud can read them.
maintenance: Clears leftovers, repairs permissions and reschedules alarms while you sleep.
diagnose: Internet, DNS and why an app stopped, all at once and in sentences you can understand.
scoreboard: The TV measures its own numbers (time to open, crashes, alarms on time) and shows them on one screen. Nothing leaves your home.
System › How this TV is doing.
safe-mode: If a new version misbehaves right after installing, the TV falls back to a safe mode and shows the way out.
whats-new: Each version explains what changed and brings a short checklist to try with the remote.
report: Tell what happened with the remote or from the phone; the TV gathers what's needed, nothing personal.
languages: Portuguese, English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Russian, Polish, Turkish, Japanese, Chinese, Korean, Hindi, Indonesian and Arabic, with right-to-left screens. It follows the TV's language.
Changes with the TV by itself.
text-size: Normal, Large or Larger, on every screen, tested so text never gets cut or overlaps.
simple-mode: Big cards, fewer things on screen and the app's name spoken aloud. For people who find the remote hard.
read-aloud: The TV says what's in focus, with navigation sounds so you know where you are.
contrast: Text at a 7:1 contrast ratio and every screen readable by Android's screen reader.
no-ads: Not on the free plan, not one sponsored pick. The screen is yours.
no-tracking: No account, no usage analytics and no crash report leaving without you sending it.
pin: Anything that changes the TV asks for a PIN, and actions that delete something ask again. Too many wrong tries? The wait grows each time.
private-dns: Pick a secure DNS (DNS over TLS); if it doesn't answer, the TV goes back to the previous one by itself.
usage: How much internet each app used and who it talked to, kept on the TV for 7 days.

dev_page.title: Developers · Sofaly
dev_page.description: Put your Android TV app's card on the Sofaly home screen. No SDK, no fee.
dev_page.h1: Your app on the home screen people actually look at.
dev_page.lead: A Sofaly plugin is your own Android TV app. It sends a short card and Sofaly draws it on the home screen, in large text and in the house style.
why: Up front, not in a drawer
Your card sits on the home screen, where the family looks every time the TV turns on, not lost in a list of apps.
One ContentProvider and one row of data. No library of ours to install, no fee to pay.
Publish on Play however you like, free or paid. Sofaly only draws the card; the app and the customers are yours.
dev_page.can_title: What you can build beyond ours
can: Water off tomorrow, 9 am to noon.
Deal of the day: 20% off coffee.
dev_page.step1: Declare a provider with Sofaly's action
dev_page.step2: Answer with one row: title, value, detail and color
rules: You never draw on the home screen: you send text and a color, Sofaly draws.
Sofaly never sends you anything about the person's apps, accounts or what they watch.
Plugins are part of the Pro plan, and the person chooses which ones show.
dev_page.soon_text: Background plugins and a plugin showcase right on the TV.
dev_page.template_text: Two sample apps you can build today: a countdown to a date the person picks on the TV, and today's moon phase. No internet, no account. MIT No Attribution: copy it, rename the package, publish.
